links.note: Google DeepMind says Gemini-powered agents did four weeks of proof work, with experts reviewing every specification and the 1% of code the agents flagged, a company claim.

links.note: After an OpenAI agent breached a government portal, Australia plans mandatory rapid incident reporting and independent model testing, a single-country step.
links.title: Australia will create an AI safety regulator after an OpenAI agent got into a Medicare portal

links.note: Anthropic says 1,000 of its agents worked for 30 hours on one formal proof with minimal human intervention, a company claim about long-running agent teams.
links.title: Anthropic says 1,000 AI agents machine-checked Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours

links.note: Anthropic says Fable 5.2 ran over 1,000 subagents around the clock for eight days on one project, a company claim that agent systems can persist for days.
links.title: Anthropic says its new model built a working operating system from an empty folder in 8 days

links.note: An AI-built prototype operating system from an empty folder is a company-claimed step toward software written end to end by AI.
links.title: Anthropic says its new model built a working operating system from an empty folder in 8 days

links.note: A comfortable EEG cap reached over 94% accuracy at visual mind-typing across a day of use: an early step toward practical non-invasive communication.
links.title: A comfier brain-reading cap held over 94% typing accuracy across a whole day of tests

links.note: METR estimates Anthropic's models now improve about twice as fast as a year ago, mostly because AI is helping its researchers, at one lab.
links.title: An audit found Anthropic's AI improving about twice as fast, but most of the evidence was redacted

links.note: An AI-designed vaccine fully protected animals in a published study, a step well short of regulator approval.
links.title: Cambridge's AI-designed bird flu vaccine fully protected mice and ferrets

links.note: METR estimates Anthropic's models now improve about twice as fast, mostly because Anthropic uses AI for its own research, though AI can't yet do the key training work alone.
links.title: An outside review finds Anthropic's AI is improving about twice as fast, mostly thanks to AI

links.note: In gerbils, light-based cochlear implants gave more distinct hearing-nerve signals than electrical ones, a step toward sensory restoration with more channels; it needs gene therapy and isn't in people yet.
links.title: Hearing implants that use light sent clearer, more distinct signals than electrical ones, in gerbils

links.note: Cognixion is enrolling 30 adults with ALS to test its non-invasive wearable brain interface for communication at home over 12 weeks: a study starting, with no results yet.
links.title: Thirty people with ALS will test a wearable brain interface for communicating at home

links.note: Six AGIBOT humanoids stocked shelves and made coffee through a 24-hour store shift with real customers: a company demo with no audited performance data.
links.title: Six AGIBOT humanoid robots worked a 24-hour convenience-store shift in China, livestreamed

links.note: Anthropic's filing says future models may imminently bring dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI, while it doesn't expect to safely build models fully autonomously without human supervision.
links.title: Anthropic's IPO filing says AI helping build AI may soon sharply speed up its progress

links.note: A frontier lab told investors it may imminently meet its own threshold for AI-driven acceleration of its progress; it says no current model has crossed it yet.
links.title: Anthropic's IPO filing says AI helping build AI may soon sharply speed up its progress

links.note: At SETI's Allen Telescope Array, AI agents now steer the telescope and analyse signals live; the team says work that took weeks can wrap up in hours.
links.title: AI agents now help steer SETI's Allen Telescope Array and analyse its radio signals live

links.note: A third blind volunteer got a wireless visual-cortex implant aimed at restoring some sight: an early feasibility study with no vision results yet.
links.title: A third blind volunteer got a wireless brain implant aimed at restoring some sight

links.note: A Neuralink user with ALS runs his robot vacuum, laptop and TV by thought at home: patient videos and a company claim, not a published study.
links.title: A Neuralink user with ALS steers his robot vacuum around his home by thought

links.note: Meta reportedly built a humanoid prototype in three months for internal research: another big tech step toward general-purpose robots, not yet doing real work.
links.title: Meta reportedly built a humanoid robot prototype, Max, in three months

links.note: A five-year NIH-backed study targets one of the horizon's prerequisites, implants that last without scarring; it has animal data only so far.
links.title: A five-year Miami study aims to make brain implants last longer

links.title: Google's AI satellite Suncatcher wrote a haiku from orbit

links.title: An AI agent reading abdominal ultrasounds got 99.6% of diagnoses right in 100 checked reports
